report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a content-moderation/content-classification model (a safety/domain taxonomy classifier), i.e., to detect/label unsafe or sensitive categories such as hate/harassment, violence, sexual/adult content, and other topical categories.

Why I think this:
- Vocabulary directions the difference points toward are dominated by safety-/moderation-relevant tokens:
  - Hate/violence/abuse: “hate”, “hated”, “punches”, “destruction”, “graves”, “rifles”, “hunters”, “slavery”, “deadly”, “captivity”.
  - Sexual/adult/celebrity: “Playboy”, “TMZ”, “homosexual”, “Palin”, “Westbrook”, “fucking”.
  - Risk/hazard/health: “asbestos”, “hydrocarbon”, “landfill”, “dumpster”, “herpes”, “iasis”.
  - Tech/media/topic-taxonomy terms: “HDTV”, “MPEG”, “Computation”, “File”, “Video”, “DJI”, “AdWords”.
  These look exactly like the label space and trigger words used in web/content filtering and ad-safety taxonomies (IAB-style categories).
- The effect is strongest at p0 across nearly all layers and grows through late layers for p1–p4, consistent with a model that “reads” arbitrary text and builds a late-layer content-category signal (rather than changing general next-token modeling). Very large BOS (p0) offsets are typical of a learned “system” objective (here: moderation/classification) applied across inputs.
- Repeated header-like tokens at later layers/positions — “Summary”, “Outcome”, “File”, “Computation”, “Students”, “Maximum”, “Amounts” — suggest structured, label-ish outputs rather than freeform generation, fitting a classifier/reporting style rather than ordinary LM continuation.
- Early-layer p0 also leans to discourse/meta tokens like “Basically”, “Consider”, “arguments”, which often accompany evaluative/judgment tasks (again pointing to classification/judgment rather than vanilla next-token prediction).

Taken together, the difference patterns match a finetune that makes Model B behave as a content-moderation/category classifier (safety-tuned to detect/label sensitive topics), rather than a general-purpose generator.
